QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_27

question.text: In the Alpha Fund worked example, after returning paid-in capital and hurdle to LPs, the GP catch-up is 25%. Distributable cash flow above hurdle is INR 5,468 crore (i.e., 6840 - 1372). The GP catch-up amount is:

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Step 10 of the worked case: Catch-up = 25% × (Distributable Cash Flow − Hurdle to Investors) = 25% × (6840 − 1372) = 25% × 5468 = INR 1,367 crore. (After catch-up, the residual INR 4,101 cr splits 80:20 LP:GP, i.e., INR 3,280.8 cr to LP and INR 820 cr carry to GP, summing GP take to INR 2,187.2 cr.) The Trap: INR 547 cr is 10% — wrong percentage. INR 4,101 cr is the post-catch-up residual, not the catch-up itself. INR 2,187 cr is the TOTAL GP distribution (catch-up + carry), not the catch-up alone. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C, XIX-A test waterfall mechanics. XXI-B PMS uses HWM-crystallisation — different from PE catch-up. Manager's Pro-Tip: In the PPM, show LPs a 'catch-up economics' example: 25% catch-up gives GP a 40% effective share of excess return (vs 20% without catch-up) — transparency pre-empts disputes at wind-up.
